title: Your day, in detail
job: Longer habitual narration with sequencing words
verifiedBy: LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: A preposition in Arabic holds a NOUN, never a verb. Where English says "after I eat", Arabic names the eating: baʿda al-futūr. The noun a verb turns into is its maṣdar, its verbal noun, and that move is the grammar of this module.

A maṣdar is vocabulary, not a formula. nāma gives an-nawm, adhhab gives adh-dhahāb, waṣala gives al-wuṣūl — and nothing in the three letters tells you which shape comes out. Each one is learned beside its verb, the way a broken plural is learned beside its singular.

baʿda and qabla put the noun after them in the GENITIVE, the case every preposition takes. This course writes no case endings, so nothing changes on the page — it is named here because it is the first time the ladder has needed the word at all.

Every frequency word ends in a written -an: dāʾiman, ʿādatan, aḥyānan, nādiran, abadan. That tail is the adverbial accusative — the same tail on L1's shukran, kathīran and qalīlan — and it is what turns a noun into an adverb.

There is no Arabic word for "never". abadan is "ever", and the negative lā stands in front of the verb: lā adhhab ilā as-sūq abadan. English packs both halves into one word, so the lā is exactly what an English speaker leaves out.

The sequencing spine is awwalan … thumma … baʿda dhālika … akhīran, and it lands where English lands it. thumma, lākin and ayḍan are already yours from L1-M10, so only the three new markers are spent here and the rest of the module goes on length.

sentences.cue: After work, I go to the market

words.note: "After", and what follows it has to be a NOUN: baʿda al-ʿamal. English can put a whole clause behind "after"; baʿda cannot hold a verb at all.

sentences.trap: English lets a clause follow "after" — after I finish work. Only a noun follows baʿda, so the verb has to become a noun first.
sentences.sound: BAʿ-da al-ʿA-mal — two ʿayns in a row, the throat-squeeze of L1-M4's ʿamal, and baʿda runs straight into its noun with no pause.

variations.cue: After work, I go home
variations.changed: the destination only: as-sūq → al-bayt

variations.cue: After school, I go to the market
variations.changed: the noun baʿda is holding: al-ʿamal → al-madrasa

mistake.display: baʿda adhhab ilā al-ʿamal, ashrab al-qahwa
mistake.script: بعد أذهب إلى العمل، أشرب القهوة
mistake.why: This is English's "after I go to work" translated word for word. baʿda cannot hold adhhab; the going has to be named as a noun: baʿda adh-dhahāb ilā al-ʿamal.

sentences.usage: The sentence that opens half of any account of a day. Swap the noun after baʿda and it carries the rest of the week.
sentences.mnemonic: baʿda wants a thing, never a doing.

sentences.cue: After breakfast, I drink the coffee

words.note: Breakfast — the noun Arabic reaches for where English says "after I eat": baʿda al-futūr. Its verb is not on this ladder, so learn the noun on its own.

sentences.trap: "After breakfast" and "after I eat breakfast" are one Arabic sentence, and it is the shorter one: the noun already carries the meal and the eating.
sentences.sound: BAʿ-da al-fu-TOOR — the ū is long and held, the stress sitting on it.

variations.cue: After breakfast, I go to work
variations.changed: the second half: what follows the meal

variations.cue: After breakfast, I drink the tea
variations.changed: the drink only: al-qahwa → ash-shāy

mistake.why: "After I eat" is the English shape and baʿda will not take ākul. Arabic names the meal instead: baʿda al-futūr.

sentences.usage: The most ordinary line in the module, and the one to say aloud until the noun comes before the verb does.
sentences.mnemonic: al-futūr is the meal that breaks the fast — a thing, so baʿda can hold it.

sentences.cue: Before sleeping, I drink the milk

words.note: "Before", and baʿda's mirror in every way, including the one that matters: it holds a noun. English's "before sleeping" has a verb inside it; qabla an-nawm has none.
The sleep — the maṣdar of L1-M9's anām. The n of nawm is a sun letter, so al- becomes an-, exactly as in an-niṣf.

sentences.trap: There is no -ing form in Arabic to put behind qabla. "Before sleeping" is "before the sleep", and the article stays on.
sentences.sound: QAB-la an-NAWM — qāf from the back of the throat, and the nawm ends on a w that glides rather than a hard m start.

variations.cue: Before sleeping, I talk with my friend
variations.changed: what fills the evening: drinking becomes talking

variations.cue: Before work, I drink the milk
variations.changed: the noun after qabla: an-nawm → al-ʿamal

mistake.why: anām is a verb and qabla holds only nouns. The noun of anām is an-nawm: qabla an-nawm, ashrab al-ḥalīb.

sentences.usage: The last line of a day, and the frame every bedtime habit hangs on.
sentences.mnemonic: anām is what I do; an-nawm is the thing I do it into.

sentences.display: ʿādatan adhhab ilā al-ʿamal fī as-sāʿa ath-thāniya
sentences.script: عادةً أذهب إلى العمل في الساعة الثانية
sentences.cue: I usually go to work at two o'clock
sentences.literal: Usually I-go to the-work at the-hour the-second

words.note: "Usually", wearing the written -an tail of L1-M4's dāʾiman and aḥyānan. It stands at the front and the verb behind it does not move.

sentences.trap: English hides the frequency word inside the verb phrase — I usually go. Arabic puts it in front of the whole sentence and leaves the verb exactly as it was.
sentences.sound: ʿAA-da-tan — the tāʾ marbūṭa of ʿāda is sounded here as a t, because the -an tail is sitting on it.

variations.display: dāʾiman adhhab ilā al-ʿamal fī as-sāʿa ath-thāniya
variations.script: دائمًا أذهب إلى العمل في الساعة الثانية
variations.cue: I always go to work at two o'clock
variations.changed: ʿādatan → dāʾiman: usually becomes always, and L1-M4's word does the job

variations.display: ʿādatan adhhab ilā al-madrasa fī as-sāʿa ath-thāniya
variations.script: عادةً أذهب إلى المدرسة في الساعة الثانية
variations.cue: I usually go to school at two o'clock
variations.changed: the destination only: al-ʿamal → al-madrasa

mistake.why: The -an tail is not decoration. Without it, ʿāda is the noun "a custom" and the sentence has two nouns and no adverb. The adverb is ʿādatan.

sentences.usage: The answer to "when do you go to work?" when the answer is a whole week rather than one morning.
sentences.mnemonic: -an is the adverb tail: shukran, kathīran, ʿādatan.

sentences.cue: I rarely eat at the restaurant

words.note: "Rarely", with the same -an tail. The rarity is inside the word, so the verb behind it stays positive: nādiran ākul, not lā ākul.

sentences.trap: English's "rarely" quietly negates its sentence — you tag it with "do you?", not "don't you?". nādiran does no such thing: nothing else in the sentence changes.
sentences.sound: NAA-di-ran — long ā at the front, and the -ran tail short and flat.

variations.cue: I sometimes eat at the restaurant
variations.changed: nādiran → aḥyānan: rarely becomes sometimes, and L1-M4's word slots straight in

variations.cue: I rarely drink coffee in the evening
variations.changed: the habit under the same nādiran: eating out becomes evening coffee

mistake.why: "I don't rarely eat" is nonsense in English too. nādiran carries the whole meaning by itself; abadan is the only frequency word in this module that wants lā.

sentences.usage: The honest middle of a habit — more than never, less than sometimes.
sentences.mnemonic: nādir is the rare one, and it stands on its own.

sentences.cue: I never go to the market

words.note: abadan is "ever", not "never". It needs lā in front of the verb — lā adhhab … abadan — which is the pair English writes as a single word.

sentences.trap: "Never" is one English word and two Arabic ones. Drop the lā because English has nothing to drop, and abadan is left with nothing to negate.
sentences.sound: laa AD-hab … A-ba-dan — the lā is short and leans on the verb; abadan carries the sentence's last stress.

variations.cue: I never drink coffee
variations.changed: the verb and its object, inside the same lā … abadan frame

variations.cue: I never eat at the restaurant
variations.changed: the habit denied: going becomes eating out

mistake.why: This is "never" packed into one word the way English packs it. Without lā it reads as "I go to the market ever", which is not a sentence: lā adhhab ilā as-sūq abadan.

sentences.usage: The strongest thing you can say about a habit, and the lā in front is not optional.
sentences.mnemonic: abadan is "ever"; the lā is the n- of "never".

sentences.display: awwalan ashrab al-qahwa, thumma adhhab ilā al-ʿamal
sentences.script: أولًا أشرب القهوة، ثم أذهب إلى العمل
sentences.cue: First I drink the coffee, then I go to work
sentences.literal: Firstly I-drink the-coffee, then I-go to the-work

words.note: "First" as a step, not as a description: awwal ("first") with the -an adverb tail. thumma behind it is L1-M10's and needs nothing new.

sentences.trap: English's "first" is both an adjective (the first bus) and an adverb (first, I drink coffee). The -an tail is what fixes awwalan as the second of the two.
sentences.sound: AW-wa-lan — a doubled w held for a beat, then the flat -an.

variations.display: awwalan ākul al-fākiha, thumma adhhab ilā al-madrasa
variations.script: أولًا آكل الفاكهة، ثم أذهب إلى المدرسة
variations.cue: First I eat the fruit, then I go to school
variations.changed: both steps replaced, and the spine holds them unchanged

variations.display: awwalan ashrab al-qahwa, thumma ākul al-khubz
variations.script: أولًا أشرب القهوة، ثم آكل الخبز
variations.cue: First I drink the coffee, then I eat the bread
variations.changed: the second step only: going becomes eating

mistake.display: awwal ashrab al-qahwa, thumma adhhab ilā al-ʿamal
mistake.script: أول أشرب القهوة، ثم أذهب إلى العمل
mistake.why: Without the tail, awwal is an adjective hunting for a noun to describe, and there is none. The sequencing word is awwalan.

sentences.usage: The opening of any account of a day. thumma, lākin and ayḍan came with L1-M10, so this line costs one word.

sentences.display: baʿda dhālika ākul al-fākiha maʿa ṣadīqī
sentences.script: بعد ذلك آكل الفاكهة مع صديقي
sentences.cue: After that I eat the fruit with my friend
sentences.literal: After that I-eat the-fruit with my-friend

words.note: "After that", learned as one piece and landing where English lands it. dhālika is L1-M9's "that", and it is the noun baʿda is holding here.

sentences.trap: This is the one place in the module where nothing after baʿda carries al-. dhālika is definite by itself, so the article would be a second one.
sentences.sound: BAʿ-da DHAA-li-ka — dh as in "this", and the two words run together as one piece.

variations.cue: After that I go home
variations.changed: what comes next: eating becomes going home

variations.display: baʿda dhālika ashrab ash-shāy maʿa ṣadīqī
variations.script: بعد ذلك أشرب الشاي مع صديقي
variations.cue: After that I drink the tea with my friend
variations.changed: the food becomes a drink, and the company stays

mistake.why: dhālika is already definite and never takes al-. The phrase is fixed and takes nothing: baʿda dhālika.

sentences.usage: The joint in the middle of an account: awwalan … thumma … baʿda dhālika … akhīran.
sentences.mnemonic: dhālika is "that" — the thing you have already said.

sentences.display: baʿda al-wuṣūl ilā al-bayt, akhīran anām
sentences.script: بعد الوصول إلى البيت، أخيرًا أنام
sentences.cue: After arriving home, I finally sleep
sentences.literal: After the-arrival to the-house, finally I-sleep

words.note: The arriving — the maṣdar of L2-M10's waṣala. Nothing in waṣala predicts wuṣūl, so the noun is learned beside the verb rather than built from it.
"Finally", closing a sequence: akhīr ("last") with the -an tail. It is the last step of awwalan … thumma … baʿda dhālika … akhīran.

sentences.trap: "After arriving" is an -ing form, and Arabic has none to offer. baʿda al-wuṣūl is "after the arrival", a noun with its article on.
sentences.sound: BAʿ-da al-wu-ṢOOL — ṣ is the heavy s, and the whole word rounds towards the back of the mouth.

variations.display: baʿda al-wuṣūl ilā al-bayt, ākul maʿa ṣadīqī
variations.script: بعد الوصول إلى البيت، آكل مع صديقي
variations.cue: After arriving home, I eat with my friend
variations.changed: what the arrival leads to: sleeping becomes eating

variations.display: baʿda al-wuṣūl ilā al-madrasa, akhīran ashrab al-māʾ
variations.script: بعد الوصول إلى المدرسة، أخيرًا أشرب الماء
variations.cue: After arriving at school, I finally drink the water
variations.changed: the place arrived at: al-bayt → al-madrasa

mistake.why: waṣaltu is a verb, and baʿda cannot hold one however natural "after I arrived" feels. The maṣdar is what goes there: baʿda al-wuṣūl ilā al-bayt.

sentences.usage: The end of the day's account, and the one place akhīran belongs.
sentences.mnemonic: waṣala arrives; al-wuṣūl is the arrival.

sentences.display: qabla adh-dhahāb ilā al-madrasa, ākul al-khubz
sentences.script: قبل الذهاب إلى المدرسة، آكل الخبز
sentences.cue: Before going to school, I eat the bread
sentences.literal: Before the-going to the-school, I-eat the-bread

words.note: The going — the maṣdar of L1-M4's adhhab, and it keeps the verb's ilā: adh-dhahāb ilā al-madrasa. dh is a sun letter, so al- becomes adh-.

sentences.trap: The maṣdar keeps the preposition its verb had. adhhab ilā al-madrasa becomes adh-dhahāb ilā al-madrasa — the noun still goes somewhere.
sentences.sound: QAB-la adh-dha-HAAB — the l of al- has vanished into the dh, which is doubled and held.

variations.display: qabla adh-dhahāb ilā al-ʿamal, ashrab al-qahwa
variations.script: قبل الذهاب إلى العمل، أشرب القهوة
variations.cue: Before going to work, I drink the coffee
variations.changed: where the going leads: al-madrasa → al-ʿamal

variations.display: qabla adh-dhahāb ilā al-madrasa, ashrab al-ḥalīb
variations.script: قبل الذهاب إلى المدرسة، أشرب الحليب
variations.cue: Before going to school, I drink the milk
variations.changed: the meal becomes a drink

mistake.display: qabla adhhab ilā al-madrasa, ākul al-khubz
mistake.script: قبل أذهب إلى المدرسة، آكل الخبز
mistake.why: adhhab is a verb and qabla holds only nouns. The noun of adhhab is adh-dhahāb: qabla adh-dhahāb ilā al-madrasa.

sentences.usage: Arabic has a second route to "before I go" — an with a verb behind it — and this course does not use it: the maṣdar is what a speaker reaches for first.
sentences.mnemonic: adhhab is the going I do; adh-dhahāb is the going itself.
